title: Insert Interval
description: Insert a new interval into a sorted, non-overlapping list and re-merge. Single pass in three phases: before, overlapping, after. O(n).

notes: Three-phase walk: BEFORE (end < newStart), OVERLAP (start <= newEnd), AFTER. Each interval is visited once.
During overlap, take Math.min of starts and Math.max of ends — newInterval may be entirely contained.
Sortedness of the input is the whole reason this runs in O(n). Don't sort again.

questions.q: What invariant lets this run in O(n) without sorting?
options: The input list is already sorted and non-overlapping

questions.q: How do you decide an interval comes BEFORE newInterval?
options: Its start is less than newInterval's start
Its end is strictly less than newInterval's start
Its start is less than newInterval's end
questions.explain: Strict `<` because touching at the endpoint should still merge.

questions.q: During the overlap phase you update newInterval by:
options: Replacing it with the current interval
Taking Math.min of starts and Math.max of ends

questions.q: Why Math.min for the start and Math.max for the end?
options: The overlapping interval may extend newInterval on either side; you must expand, never shrink

L3.prompt: Implement `insert(intervals, newInterval)` returning the merged list after insertion. Log `JSON.stringify(insert([[1,2],[3,5],[6,7],[8,10],[12,16]], [4,8]))`.
hints: Overlap condition is `intervals[i][0] <= newInterval[1]` — touching counts.
Expand newInterval by Math.min of starts and Math.max of ends.
